title: SpiceJet Ramps Up Winter Operations Amid Sector Turbulence, Plans 100 New Daily Flights After Fleet Revival
text:
News Brief
Arjun Brij
Dec 11, 2025, 10:25 AM | Updated 10:25 AM IST

SpiceJet has announced plans to significantly expand its winter operations, with the airline preparing to add as many as 100 daily flights over the ongoing schedule period.
The move comes as domestic air travel demand rises sharply and the government attempts to stabilise the aviation sector following recent disruptions at IndiGo.
The airline said on Wednesday (10 December) that the expansion is aimed at strengthening capacity on high-traffic routes and maintaining sufficient supply across the market.
The development follows the government’s decision a day earlier to reduce IndiGo’s approved winter schedule by 10 per cent to help the carrier regain operational stability after widespread cancellations since 1 December.
“As part of this effort, we plan to introduce up to 100 additional daily flights during the current winter schedule, subject to regulatory approvals,” SpiceJet said in a statement.
Under the existing winter schedule, the airline has been cleared to operate 1,568 flights per week, roughly 224 per day, marking a 20.89 per cent increase from the 1,297 weekly flights it operated last winter.
Compared to its summer schedule of 1,240 weekly flights, the rise amounts to 26.45 per cent.
SpiceJet noted that it has strengthened its fleet over the past two months by bringing 17 aircraft back into service. This has been achieved through a combination of damp-lease arrangements and the reactivation of its own grounded planes.
“This enhanced fleet availability gives us the operational flexibility to deploy incremental capacity on high-demand routes and improve overall network resilience,” the airline said.
As of 9 December, the carrier had 32 aircraft including 28 Boeing 737s and four regional jets in active service, while 36 remained grounded, according to planespotter.net. This reflects a substantial improvement from 30 September, when only 18 aircraft were operational.
SpiceJet added that its priority through the remainder of the schedule is to induct more aircraft, increase utilisation and improve connectivity through stronger route planning.
